sentences.text: It is contended that they are entitled to 80% of the valuation report instead of the average rate.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent-acquiring body submits that exorbitant claim has been made by the appellants towards fruit-bearing trees.
No cogent evidence was led by the appellants to accept the valuation report or to claim enhancement in that regard.
It is submitted that the appellants are not entitled to the interest under Section 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 from the date of the possession.

The reliance is placed on the judgment of State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailash Shiva Rangari [2016 AIR (Bom.)141].

sentences.text: I have considered rival submissions of the parties.

The lands in question are acquired for Minor Irrigation Project, Jamadi, Taluka Chalisgaon,
District Jalgaon.

The S.L.A.O granted rate of Rs.1,25,000/- per Hector which is enhanced by the Reference Court to Rs.5,00,000/- per Hector for Jirayat land and 10,00,000/- per Hector for Bagayat land in respect of the compensation  (3) 143 FA 3627 OF for trees.
The method of average rate is made applicable which is sought to be challenged in the present appeals.
6. The appellants have no grievance in respect of the rate awarded to the lands.

The respondent-acquiring body has not preferred any appeal against the impugned judgment and award.
No evidence was laid by the respondent before the Reference Court.
The oral evidence was laid by the appellants in respect of their claim.
The private valuer was examined and its report was brought on record.
The valuation report was proved by leading evidence.
There is no reason to discard the report.
9. The existence of the trees has not been disputed.
The compensation for the trees was awarded by average rate.
The method adopted by the Reference Court is perverse and causing prejudice to the appellants.

Learned counsel for the appellants has placed reliance on the judgment of Chindha Fakira Patil (supra) as well as Shaikh Noor s/o Shaikh Shabu vs. State of Maharashtra and Another reported in (2020) 6 Mah LJ 501.

sentences.text: If that is the situation then the Reference Court adopted discriminatory approach in depriving the appellants from 80% of the valuation report to the extend of trees.
It is desirable to allow the appeals.
12. It needs to be clarified that the notification under Section 4 was issued on 22.02.2007.
Award was passed on 24.04.2008.
Possession of the land was taken on 01.04.1999.
In the text of the impugned judgment, it is not made clear as to whether the possession was taken over by resorting to emergency clause of Section 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Even if the  (5) 143 FA 3627 OF 2023 possession was taken on 01.04.1999 without resorting to emergency clause,
the appellants would be entitled to rental compensation.
It would be open for them to take recourse to appropriate remedy for the same.

First Appeals are allowed partly.
b. The appellants are entitled to receive compensation for trees to the extent of Rs.80% of the report of private valuer and accordingly enhancement be given for the compensation for trees. c.

opennyai_summary.decision:
ORDER  a.
First Appeals are allowed partly.
b. The appellants are entitled to receive compensation for trees to the extent of Rs.80% of the report of private valuer and accordingly enhancement be given for the compensation for trees. c.
The appellants shall be entitled to the interest under Section 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 as per State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailash Shiva Rangari [2016 AIR (Bom.)141]. d.
The appellants shall be at liberty to claim rental compensation by resorting to appropriate procedure and the claim shall be decided on its merit expeditiously.
e. Save and except above, the impugned judgment and award shall stand unaltered.
f. The appellants shall not be entitled to the interest and statutory benefits for the delayed period.
g. 
The appellants shall pay deficit court fees.
h. Award be drawn accordingly.
